games.title: Anatomy and Biochemistry of the Eye: quick quiz
games.topic: Anatomy and Biochemistry of the Eye
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 1 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which metabolic pathway accounts for the majority of glucose utilization to generate ATP in the crystalline lens?
questions.explanation: The lens lacks mitochondria in its central fiber cells and relies on anaerobic glycolysis for approximately 80-85% of its ATP production.

questions.q: In diabetic patients, excess glucose in the lens is converted into sorbitol by which enzyme, contributing to osmotic swelling and cataract formation?
questions.explanation: Aldose reductase reduces excess intracellular glucose to sorbitol, which accumulates due to poor membrane permeability and slow conversion to fructose.

questions.q: The Pentose Phosphate Pathway (HMP shunt) is highly active in the corneal epithelium primarily to generate which molecule essential for lipid synthesis and glutathione reduction?
questions.explanation: The hexose monophosphate shunt produces NADPH, which is critical for maintaining reduced glutathione to protect ocular tissues against oxidative damage.

questions.q: Photoreceptors in the retina consume high levels of glucose and convert much of it to lactate even in the presence of adequate oxygen. What is this metabolic phenomenon called?
questions.explanation: The Warburg effect describes aerobic glycolysis, a metabolically demanding process characteristic of retinal photoreceptors and tumor cells.

questions.q: Prolonged corneal hypoxia, such as from contact lens wear during sleep, leads to an accumulation of which metabolite in the corneal stroma, inducing osmotic corneal edema?
questions.explanation: Under hypoxic conditions, the corneal epithelium shifts to anaerobic metabolism, leading to stromal lactate accumulation and subsequent osmotic swelling.

questions.q: Which glucose transporter (GLUT) isoform is predominantly expressed in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) to transport glucose across the outer blood-retinal barrier?
questions.explanation: GLUT1 is the main glucose transporter expressed in endothelial cells of the blood-retinal barrier and the retinal pigment epithelium.

questions.q: Active secretion of aqueous humor by the ciliary body epithelium relies heavily on ATP driven by Na+/K+-ATPase. Which pathway primarily supplies this ATP in the ciliary body?
questions.explanation: The non-pigmented ciliary epithelium contains high concentrations of mitochondria and relies mainly on aerobic oxidative phosphorylation for ATP production.

questions.q: Diabetic cataract development occurs partly because the rate of sorbitol synthesis by aldose reductase exceeds its rate of oxidation to fructose by which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Sorbitol dehydrogenase converts sorbitol into fructose, but its relatively low activity in the lens leads to intracellular sorbitol entrapment.

questions.q: In the human retina, major stores of glycogen utilized during transient hypoglycemia or ischemia are predominantly localized within which cell type?
questions.explanation: Müller glia serve as the main glycogen reservoirs in the retina, breaking down glycogen to supply lactate and glucose to neighboring neurons during stress.

questions.q: Deficiency in which rate-limiting enzyme of the pentose phosphate pathway increases ocular susceptibility to oxidative stress and cataractogenesis?
questions.explanation: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase is the rate-limiting enzyme of the hexose monophosphate shunt, vital for generating protective NADPH in ocular tissues.

games.title: Pneumonia: quick quiz
games.blurb: Quiz for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which microorganism is the most common overall cause of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) in adults?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the leading cause of community-acquired pneumonia across all adult age groups.

questions.q: A 68-year-old male presents with pneumonia. His blood urea nitrogen (BUN) is 8 mmol/L (22.4 mg/dL), respiratory rate is 32/min, blood pressure is 85/50 mmHg, and he is fully oriented. What is his CURB-65 score?
questions.explanation: The patient receives 1 point each for age >= 65, urea > 7 mmol/L, respiratory rate >= 30/min, and blood pressure < 90/60 mmHg, giving a total CURB-65 score of 4.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with severe pneumonia, hyponatremia, high fever, and diarrhea after staying at a hotel with a hot tub. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.explanation: Legionella pneumophila classically presents with severe pneumonia accompanied by gastrointestinal symptoms, hyponatremia, and a history of exposure to contaminated water systems.

questions.q: A 52-year-old male with chronic alcohol use disorder presents with fever, severe dyspnea, and cough producing thick, red 'currant jelly' sputum. Chest X-ray reveals a cavitating right upper lobe infiltrate with a bulged fissure. What is the most likely pathogen?
questions.explanation: Klebsiella pneumoniae pneumonia classically presents with red 'currant jelly' sputum and upper lobe cavitating pneumonia with a bulging fissure, most commonly in chronic alcoholics.

questions.q: A bedbound patient with severe neurogenic dysphagia aspirates while lying supine. Which lung segment is most commonly affected by aspiration pneumonia in the supine position?
options: Anterior segment of the upper lobe
Superior segment of the lower lobe
Medial segment of the middle lobe
Apical segment of the upper lobe
questions.explanation: When lying supine, gravity directs aspirated material preferentially into the superior segments of the lower lobes or the posterior segments of the upper lobes.

questions.q: Which oral antibiotic is recommended as first-line empiric monotherapy for an uncomplicated outpatient with community-acquired pneumonia who has no comorbidities or risk factors for resistant pathogens?
questions.explanation: High-dose oral amoxicillin is recommended as first-line empiric monotherapy for uncomplicated community-acquired pneumonia in outpatients without significant comorbidities.

questions.q: A 20-year-old college student presents with a non-productive cough, low-grade fever, fatigue, and bilateral patchy reticular infiltrates on chest X-ray. Laboratory testing demonstrates elevated cold agglutinin titers. Which organism is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a common cause of atypical pneumonia in young adults and is frequently associated with IgM cold agglutinins.

questions.q: A 72-year-old male is recovering from influenza infection when he suddenly develops high fever, worsening cough with purulent sputum, and dyspnea. Sputum Gram stain reveals Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which organism is the most likely cause of this secondary bacterial infection?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus, identifiable as Gram-positive cocci in clusters, is a classic cause of severe secondary bacterial pneumonia following a primary influenza infection.

questions.q: Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia (HAP) is defined as a lower respiratory tract infection that develops how long after hospital admission?
questions.explanation: Hospital-acquired pneumonia is defined as pneumonia occurring 48 hours or more after hospital admission that was not incubating at the time of admission.

questions.q: Which set of physical examination findings over the affected lung area is most characteristic of lobar consolidation?
options: Decreased tactile fremitus, hyperresonance to percussion, vesicular breath sounds
Increased tactile fremitus, dullness to percussion, bronchial breath sounds
Increased tactile fremitus, hyperresonance to percussion, absent breath sounds
Decreased tactile fremitus, dullness to percussion, diminished breath sounds
questions.explanation: Lobar consolidation enhances sound transmission through dense fluid-filled tissue, resulting in increased tactile fremitus, dullness to percussion, and bronchial breath sounds.

games.title: Pharmacology Examination: case showdown
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 3 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 68-year-old male with atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease presents with nausea, visual halos, and fatigue. An electrocardiogram reveals ventricular bigeminy. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment for this patient's drug-induced toxicity?
questions.explanation: Digoxin-specific antibody fragments are the definitive antidote for severe, life-threatening digoxin toxicity presenting with cardiac arrhythmias.

questions.q: A 45-year-old agricultural worker is brought to the emergency department with severe lacrimation, salivation, diarrhea, bronchospasm, and bradycardia. Physical examination reveals pinpoint pupils and muscle fasciculations. Which of the following medications should be administered immediately to reverse the muscarinic effects of this toxicity?
questions.explanation: Atropine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist used immediately to reverse life-threatening muscarinic symptoms caused by organophosphate toxicity.

questions.q: A 52-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus is prescribed a new glucose-lowering medication. She returns three weeks later complaining of recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis and increased urinary frequency, but her glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level has improved. Which of the following drug classes is most likely responsible for her symptoms?
questions.explanation: SGLT2 inhibitors increase renal glucose excretion, which lowers blood glucose levels but predisposes patients to mycotic genital infections.

questions.q: A 28-year-old female with major depressive disorder managed with sertraline presents to the emergency department after taking an over-the-counter cough suppressant containing dextromethorphan. She exhibits agitation, hyperreflexia, inducible clonus, diaphoresis, and a temperature of 38.8°C (101.8°F). What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Serotonin syndrome results from combined serotonergic drug action (e.g., SSRI and dextromethorphan) and presents with neuromuscular excitability, autonomic instability, and altered mental status.

questions.q: A 34-year-old male receiving treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis develops numbness and tingling in a 'glove-and-stocking' distribution in his extremities. He has been taking isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for two months. Which of the following co-prescriptions would have prevented this complication?
questions.explanation: Isoniazid promotes pyridoxine deficiency by inhibiting its active metabolite formation, causing peripheral neuropathy that can be prevented by Vitamin B6 co-administration.

questions.q: A 58-year-old male with hypertension presents to the clinic with severe pain and swelling in his left first metatarsophalangeal joint, consistent with acute gout. A review of his medications reveals a recently initiated antihypertensive drug. Which of the following antihypertensive agents is most likely responsible for precipitating this attack?
questions.explanation: Thiazide diuretics such as hydrochlorothiazide inhibit renal uric acid excretion, elevating serum uric acid levels and triggering acute gout flares.

questions.q: A 62-year-old female with severe congestive heart failure is admitted with acute pulmonary edema. She receives a rapid intravenous bolus of a high-dose diuretic, which quickly relieves her dyspnea but causes transient hearing impairment. Which diuretic class is associated with this adverse effect?
questions.explanation: Loop diuretics like furosemide can cause ototoxicity, particularly when administered rapidly at high intravenous doses.

questions.q: A 24-year-old female with asthma presents for a routine follow-up. She reports using her short-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler four days per week and waking up twice a month with nocturnal coughing, indicating persistent symptoms. What is the most appropriate next step in her pharmacotherapy?
options: Add a leukotriene receptor antagonist as monotherapy
questions.explanation: Adding a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid is the standard first-line controller therapy for patients with persistent asthma inadequately managed with short-acting beta-agonists alone.

games.title: Common Discomforts of Pregnancy and Their Management: case showdown
games.topic: Common Discomforts of Pregnancy and Their Management
games.blurb: Case Showdown for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 26-year-old G1P0 woman at 8 weeks of gestation presents with persistent nausea and occasional vomiting for 2 weeks. She has been unable to tolerate large meals but has no signs of dehydration, weight loss, or electrolyte imbalance. What is the most appropriate first-line pharmacotherapy if dietary modifications fail?
questions.explanation: Doxylamine combined with pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is recommended as the first-line pharmacological treatment for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy when conservative dietary measures fail.

questions.q: A 31-year-old G2P1 woman at 28 weeks of gestation presents with a 3-week history of retrosternal burning discomfort, particularly after meals and when lying flat. She has tried eating smaller meals and elevating her head at night without adequate relief. What is the next best step in management?
questions.explanation: When lifestyle modifications fail to control heartburn in pregnancy, antacids or alginates are the initial recommended pharmacotherapy.

questions.q: A 28-year-old G1P0 woman at 18 weeks of gestation complains of hard, infrequent bowel movements occurring twice per week for the past month. Physical examination is unremarkable, and she reports no rectal bleeding, fever, or severe abdominal pain. What is the most appropriate initial management step?
options: Increase dietary fiber and fluid intake
questions.explanation: Initial management of mild, uncomplicated constipation in pregnancy focuses on non-pharmacological measures, such as increasing dietary fiber and daily fluid intake.

questions.q: A 29-year-old G2P1 woman at 32 weeks of gestation presents with sharp pain over the pubic symphysis that radiates to her inner thighs. The pain is exacerbated by walking, climbing stairs, and turning over in bed, and palpation of the pubic symphysis yields local tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain (formerly symphysis pubis dysfunction) characteristically causes localized tenderness over the pubic symphysis and difficulty with weight-bearing or asymmetrical movements.

questions.q: A 33-year-old G1P0 woman at 30 weeks of gestation presents with numbness, tingling, and pain in her thumb, index, and middle fingers of both hands, which worsens at night. Physical examination reveals a positive Tinel sign at the wrist bilaterally. What is the next best step in management?
options: Wrist splinting in a neutral position
questions.explanation: Conservative management with neutral wrist splinting is the preferred first-line treatment for pregnancy-induced carpal tunnel syndrome.

questions.q: A 24-year-old G1P0 woman at 20 weeks of gestation presents with sudden, sharp bilateral lower abdominal and groin pain triggered by standing up quickly. Vital signs are normal, the uterus is non-tender, and fetal heart tones are reassuring. What is the most appropriate management?
questions.explanation: Round ligament pain is a benign discomfort of the second trimester caused by stretching of the round ligaments, requiring reassurance and conservative measures like slow position changes.

questions.q: A 30-year-old G2P1 woman at 34 weeks of gestation presents with bilateral lower leg swelling and heavy, aching sensations in her legs by the end of the day. Her blood pressure is 112/70 mmHg, urine dipstick is negative for protein, and examination shows mild bilateral non-pitting pedal edema without focal tenderness. What is the most appropriate management?
options: Leg elevation and graduated compression stockings
questions.explanation: Physiologic leg edema in late pregnancy is managed conservatively with leg elevation, periodic rest, and graduated compression stockings, while diuretics are generally avoided.

questions.q: A 27-year-old G1P0 woman at 26 weeks of gestation presents with painful, involuntary calf muscle spasms occurring primarily at night. Physical examination shows no calf swelling, warmth, or tenderness to palpation. What is the most appropriate immediate action to relieve an active spasm?
options: Passive dorsiflexion of the foot and calf stretching
questions.explanation: Immediate relief of an acute nocturnal calf cramp in pregnancy is achieved by stretching the calf muscle via passive dorsiflexion of the foot.

games.title: Medical Biochemistry II PAPER A (MBMB 2200): drug duel
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 2 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: Which hepatic enzyme is competitively inhibited by atorvastatin to lower plasma LDL-cholesterol levels?
questions.explanation: Atorvastatin competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, preventing the rate-limiting conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate during endogenous cholesterol synthesis.

questions.q: What is the primary mechanism of action of allopurinol in the pharmacotherapy of hyperuricemia?
questions.explanation: Allopurinol and its active metabolite oxypurinol inhibit xanthine oxidase, decreasing the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid.

questions.q: Metformin lowers blood glucose in type 2 diabetes primarily by activating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Which hepatic metabolic pathway is directly suppressed as a result?
questions.explanation: Activation of hepatic AMPK by metformin suppresses the gene expression of key enzymes involved in gluconeogenesis, thereby reducing hepatic glucose output.

questions.q: Methotrexate acts as a competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR). Which biochemical cofactor synthesis is directly depleted by this action?
questions.explanation: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking the reduction of dihydrofolate to tetrahydrofolate, which is required for one-carbon transfers in purine and thymidylate synthesis.

questions.q: Which enzyme in the gastrointestinal tract is inhibited by orlistat to decrease the digestion and absorption of dietary lipids?
questions.explanation: Orlistat forms a covalent bond with the active serine site of gastric and pancreatic lipases, inhibiting the hydrolysis of dietary triglycerides.

questions.q: Empagliflozin lowers blood glucose concentrations by inhibiting a specific transport protein located in the renal proximal convoluted tubule. Which protein is targeted?
questions.explanation: Empagliflozin selectively inhibits sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) in the proximal tubule, reducing renal glucose reabsorption and inducing glucosuria.

questions.q: Through which nuclear receptor mechanism do fibrates, such as fenofibrate, lower circulating plasma triglyceride levels?
questions.explanation: Fibrates act as agonists at peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-alpha (PPAR-alpha), upregulating lipoprotein lipase expression and increasing fatty acid beta-oxidation.

questions.q: Acetazolamide causes metabolic acidosis with hyperchloremia by inhibiting carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule. What is the characteristic biochemical finding in the urine of patients taking acetazolamide?
options: Urinary acidification and loss of ammonium
Urinary alkalinization and loss of bicarbonate
questions.explanation: Inhibition of proximal tubular carbonic anhydrase by acetazolamide impairs bicarbonate reabsorption, leading to urinary alkalinization and excessive excretion of sodium bicarbonate.

games.title: Preconception Care: Preparing for a Healthy Pregnancy: drug duel
games.topic: Preconception Care: Preparing for a Healthy Pregnancy
games.blurb: Drug Duel for Year 4 and above, written fresh today.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman with epilepsy well-controlled on carbamazepine presents for preconception counseling. What daily dose of folic acid should be recommended prior to conception?
questions.explanation: Women taking anti-epileptic drugs like carbamazepine require high-dose folic acid (5 mg daily) pre-conceptually and through the first trimester to lower the increased risk of neural tube defects.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman with bipolar disorder is planning to become pregnant. Which major congenital malformation is most specifically associated with first-trimester exposure to sodium valproate?
questions.explanation: Sodium valproate is significantly teratogenic, with first-trimester exposure carrying up to a 10-fold increased risk of neural tube defects such as spina bifida.

questions.q: A 34-year-old woman with essential hypertension controlled on enalapril plans to conceive. Which antihypertensive drug should replace enalapril prior to conception to avoid fetal renal dysgenesis?
questions.explanation: ACE inhibitors and ARBs are contraindicated in pregnancy due to risks of fetal renal dysgenesis and oligohydramnios, making labetalol a preferred first-line safe alternative.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman who recently finished a course of oral isotretinoin for severe acne asks when it is safe to attempt conception. What is the minimum recommended waiting period after stopping isotretinoin?
questions.explanation: Isotretinoin is highly teratogenic, and effective contraception must be continued for at least 1 month following treatment cessation to ensure adequate drug elimination.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with a mechanical heart valve managed on warfarin presents for preconception planning. What is the primary fetal risk associated with warfarin exposure during the first trimester?
options: Fetal warfarin embryopathy (nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses)
questions.explanation: Warfarin crosses the placenta during the first trimester and can cause fetal warfarin embryopathy characterized by nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses.

questions.q: A 29-year-old woman with primary hypothyroidism managed on levothyroxine asks about medication management during pregnancy. What adjustment is typically required for levothyroxine once pregnancy is confirmed?
questions.explanation: Increased thyroid-binding globulin and metabolic demands during pregnancy typically necessitate a 25-30% increase in the levothyroxine dose to maintain normal fetal development.

questions.q: A 31-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis managed on methotrexate requests guidance on starting a family. What is the minimum recommended washout period for methotrexate prior to conception?
questions.explanation: Methotrexate is a folate antagonist with teratogenic effects that requires cessation at least 3 months prior to conception for women.

questions.q: A 27-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes attends a preconception clinic. Which pharmacological agent is considered the first-line gold standard for achieving optimal glycemic control before and during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: Insulin does not cross the placenta in significant amounts and remains the first-line gold standard medication for pre-gestational diabetes management.
